references.text: God commands Abram to walk before His face and be blameless (tam), the same Hebrew root as in Deuteronomy 18:13
Noah is described as a righteous man, blameless (tamim) in his generation, who walked with God
God's way is perfect (tamim), and His word is pure - the same concept of perfection is used
The one who walks blamelessly (tamim) and does what is right describes how to live for the Lord
Blessed are those who are blameless (tamim) in their way, those who walk in the law of the Lord
Jesus says: 'Be therefore perfect, as your heavenly Father is perfect' - a direct echo of the call to be wholehearted toward God
Paul asks that believers may be pure and blameless until the day of Christ
The goal is to present every person perfect in Christ
You shall be holy, for I, the Lord your God, am holy - a parallel call to reflect God's character
